title: Report and manage a workplace injury
summary: Take care of the person first. The reporting deadlines are short and run from when you learn of the outcome: a work-related fatality goes to OSHA within 8 hours; in-patient hospitalization, amputation, or eye loss within 24 (rule card us-fed.osha-severe-injury-reporting, osha.gov cited). Then workers' comp. Notify your carrier and get the claim form to the employee fast; state deadlines are short (California requires the DWC-1 within one working day of learning of the injury). Write the incident record while memories are fresh, plus the OSHA 300 log entry if you are covered. Plan the return to work realistically. Fix the hazard. State systems differ sharply; this is the generic shape, so check your own state's rules and fund. Nothing here is legal advice. The claim moves on the carrier's and the state's timelines.

parts.title: Care first: emergency response, the scene made safe — everything else waits for this
Check the OSHA clocks: fatality — report within 8 hours; in-patient hospitalization, amputation, or eye loss — within 24
File the OSHA report if a clock applies — by phone or the online form (state-plan states have their own channels)
Notify the workers'-comp carrier and give the employee the claim form — state deadlines are short (CA: DWC-1 within one working day of notice)
Write the incident record while it's fresh: what, where, witnesses, equipment — and the OSHA 300 log entry if you're covered
Plan return-to-work or modified duty honestly, with the employee and the carrier
Fix the hazard and document the correction — the recurrence is the lawsuit
The claim runs on the carrier's and the state's clocks — track it, don't chase it daily

metadata.trigger: Someone is hurt at work: an injury on the job just happened and reporting deadlines may already be running.
metadata.supportReason: The emergency response, the carrier conversation, and the return-to-work plan are human; an agent can draft the incident record, keep the OSHA log, and track the claim's deadlines. Treat the state-fund specifics as needs-review until checked against your state.

geoNotes.summary: RIDDOR makes certain workplace injuries reportable to the HSE — deaths and specified injuries by the quickest practicable means with the report within 10 days, over-seven-day incapacitations within 15 — through the HSE's online reporting forms.

Arbeitsunfälle run through your Berufsgenossenschaft (the DGUV accident-insurance system): the Unfallanzeige is required for injuries causing more than three days' incapacity, and serious/fatal accidents are reported immediately — the insurer then owns treatment and rehabilitation.

Declare the accident du travail to the CPAM within 48 hours (Sundays and holidays excluded) and give the employee the feuille d'accident — the declaration runs electronically and late declarations expose the employer to the costs.

The Employees' Compensation Act and the ESIC scheme carry the duties: ESI-covered units report accidents through ESIC and benefits run from there, while non-covered employment falls under the EC Act's compensation machinery — the labour ministry is the canonical start.

Work accidents route through the employer's mandatory private accident insurance, and serious or fatal accidents must also reach ACT (the labour-conditions authority) within 24 hours — ACT's portal was unreachable to our crawler, so the consolidated labour code is the committed reference.

Reporting clocks are provincial: each workers'-compensation board sets its own employer-report deadline (Ontario's WSIB gives three days), and serious incidents also go to the provincial OHS regulator — CCOHS maintains the board directory.

contextNeeded.query: what happened, to whom, how serious — and when you learned of it (the clocks run from knowledge)
your workers'-comp carrier/policy and the state you operate in
